meta.title: TriggerHub 2.0 – Closed Alpha for stream automation
meta.description: TriggerHub 2.0 is a closed-alpha Windows desktop app for streamers and creators. OBS, Spotify, and automation workflows are limited, experimental, and in active development while we stabilize this preview release.
meta.ogDescription: A Windows desktop automation tool for streamers and creators. Connect OBS, Spotify, and your tools in one local workflow hub.

header.tagline: Closed Alpha desktop automation for PC streamers

footer.productInfo: TriggerHub 2.0 is a closed-alpha Windows desktop automation tool for streamers and creators. Access is limited, OBS and Spotify adapters remain experimental, and integrations plus workflows will continue to change as we stabilize the preview build.

hero.title: TriggerHub 2.0 Closed Alpha: Automate your stream. Stay focused live.
hero.description: TriggerHub 2.0 wires OBS, Spotify, scenes, and overlays through triggers and macros so you can automate the stream start-to-clip workflow. Automations run locally with no cloud relay.
proofPoints: Desktop automation tuned for Windows stream setups
Local runtime keeps OBS, music, and clips in sync

benefits.title: Less manual work. More time actually streaming.
benefits.description: TriggerHub handles the repetitive parts of your stream setup so you can stay focused on what's in front of the camera.

features.title: Core automation, built for live setups.
features.description: The trigger engine (stream states, hotkeys, and timed events) and the macro system are available; OBS and Spotify adapters are being hardened while we add more local automation workflows such as clip capture and reactive scene routines.

workflow.title: Three steps from event to action.
workflow.description: This workflow outline shows the intended flow from event to action so you can follow each stage confidently.

extensions.title: The foundation supports more than the current scope.
extensions.description: Plugin scaffolding, clip modules, and a local runtime exist, yet only a small curated set of experimental extensions is available while we roll it out gradually.

trust.title: Built on real implementation, not mockups.
trust.description: We focus on transparency, security, and engineering rigor while the product continues to evolve.

faq.title: Straight answers about TriggerHub.
faq.description: What it is today, what's in development, and what it isn't.

items.title: No more manual switching
items.description: Set up the stream-start routine once: OBS scenes, overlays, music, and clip capture trigger together so you don’t fiddle with dozens of apps during a live show.

items.title: Runs entirely on your machine
items.description: TriggerHub has no cloud backend for automations. Everything executes locally with low latency and no external dependency, while the runtime keeps improving reliability and integration coverage.

items.title: One workflow system for your whole setup
items.description: Triggers, conditions, macros, and actions share a single workflow model you can already explore to keep OBS, Spotify, and clip tooling coordinated even as we expand the editor.

items.title: Trigger engine
items.description: Define the event that kicks off a workflow. Stream status changes, hotkeys, timed events; the engine is live while we iterate on extra event sources.
bullets: Condition checks before any action runs

items.title: Macro system
items.description: Group actions into sequences you can reuse across workflows. Run steps in order, in parallel, or conditionally; this macro system is active while additional orchestration helpers are still in progress.

items.title: Service adapters (planned & evolving)
items.description: Early adapters for OBS and Spotify live in the codebase, with Twitch status detection also available; all of them remain in active development and are not yet production-stable.
bullets: Clip modules and plugin scaffolding included

items.title: Pick your trigger
items.description: Choose the event that starts the automation, a stream going live, a hotkey, a scene change. That's your entry point.

items.title: Define the logic
items.description: Add conditions to control when the automation should continue. Chain steps into a macro that runs exactly how you configured it.

items.title: Run the action locally
items.description: The automation executes on your machine. OBS switches, Spotify plays, your tools respond with no cloud relay or added latency.

items.title: Desktop-first, not cloud-first
items.description: TriggerHub runs on your machine. There is no cloud backend in the automation execution path, and we keep that desktop focus as the product continues to evolve.

items.title: Core modules are shipped
items.description: The trigger engine, macro system, and service adapter scaffolding exist in the repository and function, though we keep refining them for broader coverage.

items.title: Local execution
items.description: Automations don't leave your machine. No keys sent to third parties, no network dependency when an action fires, so you can audit that local runtime.

items.title: Tested build pipeline
items.description: Automated tests and a production build pipeline cover both this website and the desktop codebase, yet we still welcome feedback as the system adapts.

items.title: Touch-surface control
items.description: The architecture already points toward a secondary display or tablet control surface. Soundboard-style stream control is a natural extension of the current desktop model.
bullets: Second-screen or tablet operation is a documented target direction
Soundboard workflows are referenced in project docs
Extends the desktop control model; doesn't shift it

items.title: Richer clip workflows
items.description: Clip export modules and a plugin system are already in the codebase. A more capable clip pipeline with auto-save, processing, editor integration follows naturally from there.
bullets: Clip export is already part of the repository scope
Plugin system exists as an extension point
Content tooling improvements are on the roadmap

items.title: AI-assisted post-production
items.description: The roadmap mentions AI-assisted creator workflows as a later direction. A future plugin for clip refinement, tagging, and publishing fits the existing architecture, framed as possible, not current.
bullets: Future clip cleanup and refinement workflows
Tagging and preparation before export or publishing
Built to fit into creator post-production routines

items.question: What is TriggerHub today?
items.answer: A Windows desktop automation app in early access. The trigger engine and macro system work. OBS and Spotify adapters are in the codebase and being actively developed, and alpha feedback flows through the closed-access request channel so we know what deserves more polish next.

items.question: Which integrations are working right now?
items.answer: OBS and Spotify adapters are in active development. They are present in the codebase but not yet production-stable, and this alpha concentrates on PC streaming automation flows, so expect coverage to be limited to those adapters with manual workarounds until they are hardened.

items.question: Is it a cloud product?
items.answer: No. TriggerHub runs entirely on your machine. Automations execute locally, no cloud backend, no external relay, though the alpha may surface stability gaps that alpha testers help us surface.

items.question: Which platform does it support?
items.answer: Windows x64 is the current target. Mac and Linux are not on the near-term roadmap.

cta.title: Get early access.
cta.description: TriggerHub is in active development. Access is limited. Follow the release to get notified when builds are available.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: This notice explains how personal data is processed in connection with the TriggerHub 2.0 website and closed-alpha usage.

sections.heading: 1. Controller
sections.body:
The controller under the GDPR and other applicable data protection laws is:

Alexander Posdziech
Voßort 14
21037 Hamburg
Germany

E-mail: Triggerhub@outlook.com

sections.heading: 2. Components of the service
sections.body:
TriggerHub consists of:

• A Windows desktop application (Electron) that runs locally on your machine. Configuration (triggers, macros, API tokens) and third-party access tokens (e.g. Twitch, Spotify) are stored locally and are not sent to the operator.
• A website (landing page and a closed access area with e-mail authentication) hosted on Vercel. This privacy notice primarily covers the website and its backend services.

sections.heading: 3. Hosting & server logs (Vercel)
sections.body:
The website is hosted by Vercel Inc. (440 N Barranca Ave #4133, Covina, CA 91723, USA). When you access the site, Vercel may process server log data such as IP address, date and time of request, requested URL, HTTP status code, transferred data volume, and browser/user agent.

This processing is required to deliver and secure the service. The operator has no direct access to raw logs beyond what Vercel exposes via its tools.

The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in a secure and stable service). Transfers to the United States may occur on the basis of standard contractual clauses under Art. 46 GDPR. Details can be found in Vercel’s own privacy policy.

sections.heading: 4. Registration, authentication & profile
sections.body:
Access to the closed area is restricted to selected testers. There is no public signup.

When you use the auth area, the following data may be processed:

• E-mail address
• Credentials for the closed area (password stored only as a cryptographic hash)
• Session information (signed session token)
• Optional profile data (display name, avatar URL, short bio), which is stored in a profile file on the server so it can be shown again when you sign in.

The purpose is to provide and manage the closed-alpha access and your on-site profile.

The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract or pre-contractual steps). Profile data may be retained for the duration of the closed-alpha access and will be deleted upon request unless statutory retention obligations apply.

sections.heading: 5. External APIs in the desktop app (Twitch, Spotify)
sections.body:
The desktop app can optionally connect to external services such as Twitch and Spotify. These connections are established from your local installation; tokens and configuration remain on your device.

API calls (e.g. Twitch EventSub, Spotify playback control) run directly between your machine and the respective provider. They are not proxied via servers operated by the TriggerHub project. The privacy policies of those third parties apply to that processing.

sections.heading: 6. Cookies and similar technologies
sections.body:
The website uses only technically and functionally necessary cookies:

• th_prelaunch_gate – HttpOnly cookie for enforcing a prelaunch access gate for the closed alpha.
• th_prelaunch_session – HttpOnly cookie for managing the signed-in session in the closed area.
• th_csrf – security cookie providing a CSRF token for form requests.
• sidebar_state – preference cookie recording whether the navigation sidebar is expanded or collapsed.

These cookies are used solely for security and functional purposes. No analytics, profiling, or advertising cookies are set.

The legal bases are § 25(2) TTDSG (for technically required storage in Germany) and Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in a secure and usable website). A separate cookie banner is therefore not required.

sections.heading: 7. No analytics or tracking tools
sections.body: The site does not use analytics or tracking services such as Google Analytics, Plausible, Matomo, Mixpanel, or Segment. No marketing user profiles are created.

sections.heading: 8. Storage duration
sections.body: Technical server log data at Vercel is deleted or anonymized in line with Vercel’s retention schedules. Session-related cookies expire automatically after their respective lifetimes and are actively cleared on logout. Profile data is stored for as long as the closed-alpha access is in use and is removed upon request unless longer retention is required by law.

sections.heading: 9. Your rights
sections.body:
Under the GDPR you have, in particular, the following rights:

• Right of access (Art. 15 GDPR)
• Right to rectification (Art. 16 GDPR)
• Right to erasure (Art. 17 GDPR)
• Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
• Right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR)
• Right to object to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21 GDPR)

To exercise your rights, you can contact Triggerhub@outlook.com at any time.

sections.heading: 10. Right to lodge a complaint
sections.body:
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority, in particular in the EU Member State of your habitual residence, place of work, or of the alleged infringement (Art. 77 GDPR).

For Hamburg, Germany, the competent authority is the Hamburg Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information (Hamburgischer Beauftragter für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit).

sections.heading: 11. Changes to this notice
sections.body: These privacy details may be updated as the service evolves. The date of the most recent update is shown on the website. Material changes will be communicated to signed-in testers as part of the closed alpha program.
